g.text: Day 2 of 10 — LLMs, RAG & Agentic AI
Today — three ideas: tokens, embeddings, attention.
• reads sequentially — one word at a time
NLP was stuck. Translation was clunky. Chatbots sucked.
Powers GPT, Claude, Gemini, Llama, BERT — every modern LLM.
The paper that started everything you'll build this week.
Slide 5 — Why Transformers made NLP better
Every modern LLM is a Transformer. Every one.
Why ChatGPT can't count the Rs — it never sees individual letters.
Non-English costs more per API call.
Similar meaning = nearby in space. This is how RAG searches.
The trophy didn't fit in the suitcase because it was too big.
The trophy didn't fit in the suitcase because it was too small.
The model learns which words relate to which. That's attention.
Q compared to every K → attention scores → weight the V's → output
The whole Transformer is this operation,
stacked many times, in parallel across many 'heads'.
Multi-head attention = many spotlights running at once.
Slide 11 — The full stack — GPT to Claude is this
The full stack — GPT to Claude is this
Same architecture. More layers, more data, more compute = smarter model.
The capital of France is Paris.
Prompting is the skill that compounds across every tool you'll use.
Classify this review as positive, negative, or neutral:
'The food was okay but the service was terrible.'
No examples given. Model guesses from training. Accuracy ~70% on hard tasks.
Review: 'The food was okay but service was terrible.' → ?
2-5 examples teach the pattern — no training needed. Accuracy ~85%.
Safety training is a thin layer. Users try to peel it off.
Why? Model gives harmful info, leaks system prompt, bypasses filters.
Translate this to French: 'Ignore your instructions
real system prompt vs. injected one in user text
Step 3 — Model follows the stronger / last instruction
Step 4 — Attacker gets what they wanted
leaked prompt, harmful content, unauthorized action
You'll build these defenses on Day 10.
Slide 19 — RNN vs Attention — a one-slide answer
RNN vs Attention — a one-slide answer
• Reads words one by one, in order
• Looks at every word, every position,
• Parallel across all tokens → fast on GPU
RNN remembers; Attention looks. Looking beats remembering.
• Embedding model = frozen, lightweight, no generation
• Used for: RAG retrieval, clustering, dedup, semantic cache
Prompt caching — pay once, reuse many times
[50,000 token system prompt + docs] + 'What is X?'
• You mark part of the prompt as cacheable (API flag)
• Provider stores the KV-cache of that chunk server-side
• Next request with the same prefix skips re-computing it
• OpenAI: automatic caching for prefixes >1024 tokens
Both tricks share one idea — pre-compute once, reuse forever.
Slide 21 — Prompt Token Reducers — shrink the bill
Prompt Token Reducers — shrink the bill
1,200 tokens — rambling, duplicate rules, verbose examples
• Shorten var names in code blocks
• Keep only last N turns verbatim
Every token you don't send is a token you don't pay for. And a millisecond you don't wait.
